## Grouping by turn

You're right that a group per turn would be too coarse. I looked at the stored threads (#24–#46): a workflow run usually answers 1 comment, sometimes 2–3. That one answer takes anywhere from 1 to 92 model responses, nearly always with one tool call each. A turn group would hide almost the whole run behind one fold.

So the PR uses one line per step instead, with the details folded away:

```
▸ Setup
🤖 nvidia/aws/anthropic/bedrock-claude-opus-5-5 · extensions: pit (typescript)
▸ 🧵 Thread refs/pi/threads/46: continuing, started 2026-11-12 07:11 UTC
▶ Request from @cv (https://github.com/…#issuecomment-…): Ready to write a PR?
💬 I'll look at the existing sessions first.
🔧 bash: git log --oneline -5
▸   ↳ ✓ 0.1s · 5 lines
🔧 edit: src/run.ts (2 edits)
▸   ↳ ✓ 0.0s · 1 line
▸ 💬 I opened PR #48, which …
✅ Replied: https://github.com/…#issuecomment-… (24 model responses · 23 tool calls · 6m40s · 2.1M tokens in, 31k out)
🧵 refs/pi/threads/46 is at 4325d9a
```

- **`🔧` when a tool call starts.** It shows the tool and its main argument (the command, path or label). You can see what's running while you follow the log, even during a long `npm test`.
- **`↳ ✓` or `↳ ✗ failed` when it ends.** This line shows how long the call took and how many lines it printed. It folds open to the full arguments and the last 30 lines of output. When one response makes several calls, each `↳` line names its call.
- **`💬` for the model's text.** Text longer than one line folds, with the first line as the header.
- **`▶` per request and `✅`/`❌` per reply.** The reply line has totals: model responses, tool calls, time, tokens, and cost when the provider reports it.

The data comes from the entries as they are stored, so nothing extra runs during the agent loop.
